entry.title: Exact Color Kinematics Duality in the Cosmological Correlators
entry.summary: In this paper, we study color kinematics duality and related double-copy and BCJ structures in the cosmological Grassmannian framework. The simplicity of these correlators in this framework makes it possible to test the double copy construction beyond flat space. We show that the four-point gluon correlator admits a representation whose kinematic numerators satisfy an algebraically exact Jacobi identity, $n_s$ + $n_t$ + $n_u$ = 0. Replacing color factors with kinematic numerators gives a graviton correlator that reproduces the correct factorization residues and flat-space limit, which matches with the BCFW result up to terms regular in all exchange channels. In addition, we construct a differential bi-adjoint scalar matrix whose null vector gives rise to a differential BCJ relation among color-ordered gluon correlators. We further explore an s-copy construction for general integer-spin correlators and show that for odd spin the corresponding numerators satisfy a Jacobi identity. Finally, we develop a differential representation for scalar four-point correlators with gluon exchange. These results establish algebraic and differential aspects of graviton and gluon correlators in curved spacetime.

entry.title: Few-Magnon Universality beyond Contact Interactions in Long-Range Spin Chains
entry.summary: Quantum few-body systems exhibit a rich variety of phenomena that provide fundamental insights into universality. A paradigmatic example is the Efimov effect, in which an infinite tower of three-body bound states emerges with binding energies forming a geometric sequence. Motivated by advances in trapped-ion systems, recent theoretical work has predicted that the Efimov effect can arise in certain long-range quantum spin chains, where magnons exhibit a general dispersion $ε_k=u|k|^z$ with $z\in(0.52,0.88)$ and interact through a contact potential. Nevertheless, whether Efimov universality persists in the presence of experimentally relevant long-range interactions between magnons remains unexplored. In this work, we address this issue by investigating the two- and three-magnon problems with a model interaction potential $V(x)=V_0/(1+|x|^β)$. Our results demonstrate that few-body universality persists for any $β>1$: In the two-magnon sector, the low-energy expansion of the scattering matrix near a two-body resonance agrees with the universal form predicted by contact-interaction theory. The three-magnon bound-state spectrum exhibits Efimov scaling, with a scaling factor consistent with the theory. We further highlight the experimental relevance of our model, which can be readily realized in trapped-ion systems. Our results pave the way for quantum simulations of universal few-body physics beyond the traditional paradigm of nonrelativistic particles.

entry.title: Non-perturbative news from the conformal window
entry.summary: Dynamical symmetry breaking plays a crucial role in mass and scale generation. In QCD-like theories, its dependence on the number of fermion flavours determines the phase structure and the transition to the conformal regime. In this work, we compute non-perturbative corrections relevant to this phenomenom, including momentum dependencies and field invariants essential for an adequate realisation of the global symmetries, by means of the functional renormalisation group and the generalised flow equation. We find that the critical gauge coupling required for dynamical chiral symmetry breaking acquires a strong dependence on the number of flavours and increases sharply at $N_f^\textrm{crit}\simeq 7.30$ for $N_c=3$. This establishes a new picture of the phase transition to the conformal window that disfavours Miransky/BKT scaling and walking regimes but supports a first-order quantum phase transition and a critical region with exotic dynamics and symmetric fermion mass gaps.

entry.title: The Non Parametric Reconstruction of Binary Black Hole Mass Evolution from GWTC-4.0 Gravitational Wave Catalog
entry.summary: The distribution of binary black hole (BBH) masses and its evolution with redshift provide key insights into the different formation channels of compact objects and their dependence on cosmic time and stellar properties such as metallicity and star formation history. We present a non-parametric framework of the redshift evolution of the BBH mass distribution using the gravitational-wave (GW) catalogs GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK). This method simultaneously searches for the signature of any linear and quadratic redshift evolution with respect to the low-redshift population in a Bayesian framework, taking into account the detector selection effects. We find tentative evidence for a linear redshift-dependent evolution of the mass distribution, consistent over a mass range ($m \gtrsim 50\,M_\odot$), while lower-mass systems show no significant evolution. The quadratic term remains consistent with zero, indicating that a simple linear dependence adequately describes the population up to redshift $z \sim 1$. With more GW sources in the future, this technique can reveal subtle evolutionary features in BBH populations and provide new insights into the cosmic history of black hole formation.

entry.title: Radiation-Regulated Spherical Accretion with an Inner Accretion Disk
entry.summary: We develop a theoretical model for radiation-regulated spherical accretion with an inner accretion disk. In our model, the outer accretion flow remains quasi-spherical and optically thick, while the luminosity generated by the inner disk is self-consistently coupled to the accretion rate and irradiates the inflowing gas. By solving the global transonic structure with radiative transfer treated in the diffusion approximation, we investigate how radiation regulates the flow structure and the accretion rate. We find that the luminosity is constrained by a generalized Eddington limit, leading to a saturated accretion rate typically lower than the classical Bondi prediction by orders of magnitude. At sufficiently low densities, the enthalpy flux of the spherical inflow contributes substantially to the emergent luminosity, in which case the inner disk luminosity is reduced and the accretion flow enters an unsaturated state. A criterion is derived to estimate whether the accretion flow is saturated. We further demonstrate the applicability of our model by considering fallback accretion in failed supernova systems. The predicted nearly constant emergent luminosity, constrained by the generalized Eddington limit, provides a possible explanation for the observed luminosity plateau in the failed supernova candidate M31-2014-DS1. The presence of an inner disk also provides sufficient radiation to avoid the under-luminous predictions of a purely spherical fallback model extending down to the central object. Our model provides a framework for studying radiation-regulated accretion flows in systems where low but finite angular momentum leads to the formation of an accretion disk within a larger-scale quasi-spherical inflow.

entry.title: Spiral galaxy spacetime in extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
entry.summary: In this work, using nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED) as a source in the field equations of extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet (E-STGB) gravity, a novel type of static and spherically symmetric spacetime is found. We show that this novel type of spacetime can be used to explain the rotation curves and gravitational lensing of spiral galaxies. The NLED model used to derive our solution, in the weak and strong field limits, reduces to Maxwell electrodynamics. Furthermore, for a wide range of parameter values where our solution describes the gravitational field of a spiral galaxy, the NLED model satisfies the null and weak energy conditions. Hence, our results suggest that the extended scalar-tensor-Gauss-Bonnet gravity minimally coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics (E-STGB-NLED) provides a viable alternative to explain flat rotation curves of spiral galaxies without invoking dark matter.

entry.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
entry.summary: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature. We explicitly relate HR to Topological Regularisation (TR), where the latter prescribes to add the Euler term to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian density, with a precise coefficient so as to ensure that the resulting density is polynomial in the anti de Sitter (AdS) curvature. The polynomial is still asymptotically divergent. We find that the aforementioned, unique conformal gravity action in 8D, reproduces the polynomial, together with extra boundary terms that cancel the divergent terms in the action. We conjecture that, in arbitrary even dimension, HR is equivalent to conformally completing the Einstein-Hilbert action with negative cosmological constant, plus the Euler term with fixed coupling prescribed by TR.

entry.title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
entry.summary: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

entry.title: Direct Charge-4e Superconductivity by Mobilizing Bound Quartets
entry.summary: A direct charge-\(4e\) superconductor exhibits coherent four-electron order without condensation in any charge-\(2e\) pairing channel. We establish three complementary results. First, a particle-number-conserving Hamiltonian with electron hopping and two-body interactions moves bound quartets efficiently: for electron- and pair-hopping amplitudes \(t\) and \(K\) and local gap \(U_0\), virtual pair transfer produces quartet hopping at order \(K^2/U_0\), whereas electron hopping alone contributes only at order \(t^4/U_0^3\). Second, the microscopic theory identifies an exactly solvable parent Hamiltonian at the phase-separation boundary. Its ground state combines quartet off-diagonal long-range order and finite phase stiffness without pair condensation, while rigorous bounds establish quartet order beyond the parent in a family with explicit quartet transfer. Third, a single convergent strong-coupling expansion simultaneously controls quartet kinetics and thermodynamic stability and rules out condensation in every pair channel of the microscopic model. On bipartite hypercubic lattices at half quartet filling, it yields a parametrically controlled homogeneous phase for \(d\geq2\), with quartet order, a linear collective mode, and gapped charge-\(2e\) excitations. Virtual pair transfer thus enables a direct charge-\(4e\) superconducting ground state without pair condensation.

entry.title: Cosmological Vacuum Decays from Schwinger-Keldysh Formalism
entry.summary: In this work, we take a first step to a stochastic real-time description of the vacuum phase transitions in a radiation-dominated FLRW universe from the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. By splitting the phase transition field $Φ$ into the long-wavelength mode $φ$ and the short-wavelength mode $σ$ and tracing over the latter as the environment, we obtain a classical Langevin-type equation-of-motion for the long-wavelength field $φ$, where the quantum effects are encoded in a non-Markov memory kernel and a non-Gaussian noise. As a phenomenological example, we start from a polynomial potential and a thermalized initial state, and study the structure of the memory kernel as well as the correlation functions of the noise term. Further extensions remain possible to describe the whole dynamics of cosmological first-order phase transitions via numerical simulations.

entry.title: Phantom-Divide Crossing in Barrow-Tsallis Holographic Dark Energy with a Scale-Dependent Barrow Exponent
entry.summary: Phantom-divide crossing is studied in spatially flat cosmologies with standard Friedmann equations, separately conserved holographic dark energy and a barotropic fluid, and the future event horizon as the infrared cutoff. The horizon entropy and dark-energy density are prescribed by $ S_h=S_{\mathrm{BH}}F(L) $ and $ ρ_X\propto F(L)/L^2 $, where $ F(L) $ is smooth, positive and single-valued, with $ χ=\mathrm{d}\ln F/\mathrm{d}\ln L $. For $ w_b>-1 $, $ 0<Ω_X<1 $ and $ χ<2 $ along the trajectory, at most one phantom-divide crossing is possible. If a crossing occurs, dark energy passes from the quintessence regime into the phantom regime at a maximum of the horizon radius. The crossing kinematics determines the local entropy-scaling dimension and the sign of the local Chevallier-Polarski-Linder coefficient. Integrating the locally prescribed scale-dependent Barrow exponent reconstructs the Barrow-Tsallis entropy function. A necessary and sufficient event-horizon consistency criterion selects admissible solutions, whose late-time asymptotics include de Sitter states, Type III and Big Rip singularities, and accelerated power-law expansion under the corresponding parameter conditions. A numerical comparison with a constant Barrow exponent distinguishes the occurrence of a crossing from the effect of exponent variation on late-time evolution. With an adiabatic barotropic fluid, additive total entropy and an equilibrium Gibbs relation for dark energy, the generalized second law fails at the kinematic crossing for positive barotropic-fluid entropy and finite nonzero dark-energy temperature. The divergence of $ c_a^2 $ shows that the purely barotropic adiabatic description of perturbations breaks down. This divergence alone does not establish physical instability.

entry.title: Electronic Structure of a Delafossite Oxide CuAlO$_2$ in Comparison with CuCrO$_2$
entry.summary: We investigated the electronic structure of a delafossite oxide CuAlO$_2$ in comparison with CuCrO$_2$, using vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) and hard x-ray (HX) photoemission spectroscopy (PES) and band structure calculations within the local-density approximation +$U$ scheme. Cu 3$p\! -\! 3d$ resonant PES and Cu $2p$ core-level HX-PES give concrete evidence that the Cu valence in CuAlO$_2$ is monovalent, which makes a sharp contrast to CuCrO$_2$ that showed contradictory results depending upon probing methods [Yokobori \textit{et al.}, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{87}, 195124 (2013)]. We further noticed weak but detectable satellite structures due to Cu$^{2+}$ state in the Cu $2p$ HX-PES spectrum of CuCrO$_2$, surprisingly, without an observable main peak due to the Cu$^{2+}$ state. Comparisons between the valence-band HX-PES spectra and the band structure calculations revealed a significant amount of the Cu $4s$ and Al $3s$/Cr $4s$ states in the valence band. The above results can reasonably be explained by the Cu $3d, 4s-$Cr $3d$ charge transfer model that we previously proposed in the above paper, thereby demonstrating the critical role of empty $3d$ orbitals in the electronic structure of the copper delafossite oxides.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes of rotating black holes with ultralight scalar fields
entry.summary: We report the first accurate computation of the leading-order shifts in the quasinormal-mode frequencies of rapidly rotating black holes surrounded by massive scalar fields with nonminimal curvature coupling. For fields with reduced Compton wavelengths no shorter than the black-hole mass scale, the numerical errors in the frequency shifts are typically $10^{-8} - 10^{-5}$ for dimensionless spins between 0 and 0.9, and at most $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ next to the scalar-mass threshold. Our results open up the possibility of searching for ultralight scalar particles, prime dark-matter candidates, using existing gravitational-wave signals.

entry.title: Magnetic-field-induced chaos of charged particles around a rotating black hole in a King-type dark matter halo
entry.summary: We investigate the dynamics of charged test particles around a rotating black hole embedded in a King-type dark matter halo and subjected to a prescribed, asymptotically uniform magnetic field. We adopt an effective rotating geometry constructed from a static halo seed through a modified Newman--Janis prescription and a test electromagnetic field that generally requires supporting currents in the nonvacuum background. In the absence of magnetic coupling, the timelike Hamilton--Jacobi equation separates and admits a Carter-type constant, providing an integrable reference system. We characterize the orbital dynamics using Poincaré sections and tangent-vector growth diagnostics, including fast Lyapunov indicators and finite-time Lyapunov exponents, with mass-shell monitoring and numerical refinement checks. For the sampled initial conditions, increasing the magnetic coupling can produce a transition from regular motion to scattered Poincaré sections with sustained positive finite-time growth rates. At fixed magnetic coupling, the two higher-density halo cases yield larger finite-time exponents for a representative chaotic orbit family, whereas the weak-halo correction is not resolved consistently under numerical refinement. A different initial condition yields a closed Poincaré curve and a decreasing finite-time exponent over an extended integration, supporting regular motion despite the nonzero magnetic coupling. These results show that the King-type halo modulates magnetic-field-induced orbital instability in an initial-condition-dependent manner, while regular motion persists within the magnetized system.

entry.title: Measuring higher-order bulk topology in a programmable quantum simulator
entry.summary: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. Crystalline higher-order topological insulators can extend this principle by hosting localized corner modes in two and higher dimensions. Although these boundary modes can be detected spectroscopically through the local density of states, determining the underlying bulk topology, for example through nested Wilson loops, remains an outstanding experimental challenge. Here we use up to 728 qubits in a superconducting analogue-digital quantum simulator to realize and probe a hierarchy of one-, two-, and three-dimensional topological insulators governed by effective tight-binding Hamiltonians. By reconstructing complex propagators from real-space measurements, we obtain complementary boundary and bulk characterizations: local densities of states reveal localized boundary modes, whereas experimentally reconstructed band projectors yield bulk topological invariants, culminating in a three-dimensional octupole moment extracted through third nested Wilson loops. These results establish a route to realizing, characterizing, and manipulating topologically protected states in programmable three-dimensional quantum matter.

entry.title: Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
entry.summary: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB$_6$ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time-reversal-symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB$_6$ we find that the interaction between conduction $d$- and $f$-electrons drives a surface phase transition near $T_c\approx10$ K in which the time-reversal-odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface $\overlineΓ$ and $\overline{X}$ Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time-reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB$_6$.

entry.title: Infrared Problem in Quantum Electrodynamics
entry.summary: It is well known that the inclusive cross section in QED is infrared finite. In the standard diagram techniques this result follows from cancellation of infrared divergences. We suggest a new approach that should lead to IR -safe computational technique for QED with massive fermions.

entry.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
entry.summary: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll φ_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > φ_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle φ\rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(φ) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

entry.title: Radio Morphing: Fast computation of inclined air shower radio emission
entry.summary: The preparation of the next-generation of large-scale radio experiments requires running a large number of simulations to explore multiple detector configurations over vast areas and develop novel methods for the reconstruction of air shower parameters. While Monte Carlo simulations are accurate and reliable tools, they are too computationally expensive to explore the full parameter space of these new detectors within a reasonable timescale, and faster and more efficient methods are needed. We introduce a new version of Radio Morphing, a semi-analytical tool designed to simulate the radio emission of any cosmic-ray induced air shower with zenith angle $θ>60^{\circ}$, at any desired antenna position, from the simulation data of a few reference showers at given positions. This version incorporate refined scaling laws of the radio emission with the shower zenith angle, a novel interpolation method, the implementation of the charge-excess mechanism and the possibility to enable shower-to-shower fluctuations. We present the latest performances of Radio Morphing, tuned for a GRAND-like detector, which now provides an estimation of air shower radio signals four orders of magnitude faster than standard Monte Carlo simulations, while keeping an accuracy on the peak amplitude better than $17\%$ on unfiltered traces, better than $13\%$ in the [50 - 200] MHz band, and below $\sim 10\%$ in the [30 - 80] MHz band.

entry.title: In-ice Radio Signatures of Cosmic Ray Particle Cascades
entry.summary: To detect ultra-high-energy neutrinos, experiments such as the Askaryan Radio Array and the Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland target the radio emission induced by these particles as they cascade in the ice. This is done by, amongst others, using deep in-ice antennas at the South Pole or in Greenland. A crucial step toward this goal is the characterization of the in-ice radio emission from cosmic-ray-induced particle showers. These showers form a primary background for neutrino searches, but can also be used to validate the detection principle and provide calibration signals for in-ice radio detectors. In this work, we use the Monte-Carlo framework FAERIE to perform the first characterization of cosmic ray signals with simulations that incorporate both their in-air and in-ice emissions. We investigate cosmic ray signatures such as their radiation energy, timing, polarization and frequency spectrum and quantify how they depend on shower properties. These results provide key guidelines for cosmic-ray identification and cosmic-ray/neutrino discrimination in future in-ice radio experiments.

entry.title: Probing black holes extremality bounds with non-extensive entropies
entry.summary: Due to the importance of studying quantum-gravity-induced corrections to Einstein's theory of gravity, it is of interest to consider non-extensive entropies whose potential applications include identifying such corrections. In this Letter, we investigate possible corrections to a universal relation associated with the extremality bound of the mass of a black hole by employing entropies defined as functions of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.

entry.title: Many-body effects on dense matter with hyperons at finite temperature
entry.summary: In this work, we present the first extension of the Many-Body Forces (MBF) Model to finite temperature. The MBF Model describes nuclear matter in a relativistic quantum hadrodynamics formalism that takes many-body forces into account through a field dependence of the nuclear interaction coupling constants. Assuming nuclear matter to be charge neutral, beta-equilibrated, and populated by the baryon octet, electrons, muons, and neutrinos, we explore the parameter of the model that controls many-body forces, three different hyperon coupling schemes (also introduced here for the first time in the MBF Model), and temperature effects to describe basic properties of nuclear matter, including the speed of sound, compressibility, and adiabatic index. We also investigate the mass-radius relation of neutron and protoneutron stars by solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations at zero and finite temperature, including scenarios with fixed entropy per baryon and lepton fraction. We find that different hyperon coupling schemes soften the equation of state to different degrees, requiring different degrees of many-body force effects to reproduce observations, although they are never zero. Multidimensional tables with our results are available in the CompOSE repository, ready to be used in astrophysical simulations.

entry.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
entry.summary: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

entry.title: Microscopic entropy of regular BTZ black holes in 3d Lovelock gravity at all orders
entry.summary: We give a microscopic derivation of the semi-classical entropy of the black holes of 3d Lovelock gravity with an infinite tower of regularized Lovelock corrections, which include the regular BTZ black holes found recently. Working in the mini-superspace formalism, we show that the reduced action and its boundary term can be obtained in closed form at all orders in terms of the generating function of the couplings. Assuming the ground state is described by the soliton obtained from the static black hole by a double Wick rotation, we compute the soliton mass and reproduce the semi-classical entropy from the Cardy formula without central charges for arbitrary couplings. We then extend the mini-superspace to stationary configurations, compute the mass and the angular momentum of the rotating black holes obtained by a boost, and verify the Cardy formula in the presence of rotation.

entry.title: Holographic Complexity as a Probe of Boundary Entropy in AdS/BCFT
entry.summary: We investigate how the sewing operations familiar from topological quantum field theory provide a useful organizational framework for semiclassical AdS/BCFT path integrals. Our purpose is not to identify AdS/BCFT with a topological field theory: the bulk geometry, the end-of-the-world brane, and the on-shell action remain intrinsically metric-dependent. Rather, we use the TQFT language of state preparation, orientation reversal, and gluing to separate interface data from local geometric contributions. For AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$, we review how the Euclidean on-shell action and the Ryu--Takayanagi prescription reproduce the Affleck--Ludwig boundary entropy $\log g$ after holographic renormalization. We then formulate the Complexity=Action calculation in the presence of an end-of-the-world brane, carefully distinguishing bulk, brane, joint, and null-boundary contributions. We emphasize that finite terms in a relative Wheeler--DeWitt action depend on the choice of regulator matching and on the null-boundary counterterm scheme unless their scheme independence is established explicitly. Finally, we extend the geometric construction to a planar BTZ background and derive the brane embedding from the Neumann boundary condition. The resulting framework clarifies which aspects of holographic complexity are sensitive to boundary conditions and which require further renormalization input before they can be interpreted as universal boundary data.

entry.title: From Lyapunov Growth to Weak Quantum Chaos
entry.summary: Local out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) measure the growth of initially small commutators. For bounded local operators, this growth ends when the local commutator becomes of order one, but in an extended system the region over which it is large can continue to expand. We study this spatial proliferation using three related observables: the local squared commutator $C_r(t)$, its spatial sum $\bar C(t) = \sum_r C_r(t)$, and the symmetrically regularised connected dOTOC $D(t)$ of two extensive observables. We show that Lieb--Robinson locality gives $\bar C(t) \lesssim t^d$. We then prove that, in a Gibbs state with uniform exponential clustering, the full dOTOC obeys the same bound, $D(t) \lesssim t^d$, improving our earlier suboptimal $t^{3d}$ bound. We illustrate these results in two quantum many-body systems: a Brownian coupled-cluster model and a finite-temperature SYK chain. In both cases, an exact disorder symmetry relates $D(t)$ to $\bar C(t)$ and allows us to follow the same extensive observable from the pre-scrambling Lyapunov regime into the post-scrambling growth associated with an expanding saturated region. This late-time power-law growth is the concrete realisation of the weak quantum chaos introduced in our earlier work.

entry.title: Eigenstate transitions and critical transport in 3D Aubry-André model
entry.summary: We numerically study spectral and wave-function properties, as well as time evolution, in finite-size commensurate approximations of the 3D Aubry-André model. We explicitly show, through scaling analysis, the existence of two critical points. One of the critical points is a localization-delocalization transition in real-space, similar to the critical point in the 3D Anderson model. The other is a localization-delocalization transition in a dual momentum space, which does not have any analog in the 3D Anderson model. We estimate their values from spectral measures, such as the gap ratio and the spectral form factor, as well as from wave-function measures, such as the inverse participation ratio and the participation entropy. Additionally, we demonstrate that both critical points exhibit hallmarks of critical points between quantum ergodicity and localization. First, the eigenstates and the eigenspectrum at the critical point fulfill the mutual universal relation between the eigenspectrum compressibility $χ$ and the eigenstate fractal dimension $d^{(1)}$ [S. Jiricek et al., Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 123, e2518027123 (2026)]. Second, the dynamics of the wave packet at the critical point is governed by the critical dynamical exponent $z$, characterized by the spectral fractal dimension and the dimensionality of the lattice [M. Hopjan and L. Vidmar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 060401 (2025)]. Thus, similarly to the 3D Anderson model, the critical dynamical exponent is sub-diffusive with the value of $z=3$.

entry.title: Area metric gravity à la Plebanski: connection, curvature and dynamics
entry.summary: Area metrics arise as effective description at intermediate scales in a number of approaches to quantum gravity, including string theory, holography and loop quantum gravity. Recently, it has been shown that area metric actions can be derived from the modified Plebanski framework on the linearized level. Surprisingly these actions avoid extra poles in the propagator for the effective length dynamics, and hence constitute interesting deformations of linearized Einstein gravity. To be able to study whether this property persist for the full theory, we construct here non-linear area metric dynamics from modified Plebanski actions. We provide the geometric tools for area metrics that do not rely on perturbation theory and allow a systematic construction and study of general non-linear area metric actions: an algorithm that extracts a length metric from an area metric and a connection on two-forms that is uniquely determined by the area metric, together with its curvature and curvature invariants. We derive area metric actions from modified Plebanski actions in first and second order versions. We also find that area metric actions can be reformulated as Poincare gauge theories. We determine the effective length metric action, which on a flat background describes a graviton and a massive spin-two field with parity-violating couplings set by the Barbero--Immirzi parameter. Additionally we discuss cosmological backgrounds and the role of the matter coupling, which together open the way to cosmological applications.

entry.title: Gravitational wave signatures from area metric gravity
entry.summary: Area metric theories have been proposed as effective descriptions in a number of quantum gravity approaches: as continuum limit of effective spin foams, as an effective description for string theory and in the context of holography. Area metric actions allow for non-topological parity violating terms, which opens the possibility of observationally determining the Barbero-Immirzi parameter. We consider the shift symmetric version of linearized area metric theory in Lorentzian signature, which arises in particular from spin foams and modified Plebanski theory, and avoids ghost and tachyonic instabilities in the graviton sector. We discuss the gravitational wave like solutions of this theory and through an analysis of the coupling to electro-magnetism, deduce the signals in gravitational wave detectors. Using polarized light in such interferometers allows in principle to measure area metric induced birefringence. For the non-length excitations that accompany a gravitational wave this birefringence turns out to be independent of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter; the parameter is instead encoded in the polarization structure of the massive non-length waves, where it rotates the axes of the induced birefringence. Assuming Planck massive non-length excitations in the area metric the resulting signals are however extremely weak.

entry.title: One-loop mass corrections and decay widths of Type II heavy string states
entry.summary: We approach a systematic investigation of the one-loop mass corrections to (super-)string massive higher-spin states. While the imaginary part of the relevant amplitudes is finite, being related to the width of the decay of the states into two lower-mass states at tree level, the real part is generally IR-divergent and needs regularization and renormalization. We mostly focus on states of the first Regge trajectory in the NS-NS sector of Type-II string theories. We explicitly derive a closed-form expression for the integral over the insertion point, relying on properties of elliptic functions and lattice sums. We then regularize the IR divergent integral over the modular parameter of the torus, applying the $i\varepsilon$-prescription in string theory. As a result we compute the desired mass corrections up to level $N = 10$ and analyze their behavior at increasing $N$. Finally, we speculate on the existence of mixing among lower-spin states and conjecture that the one-loop mass matrix be governed by some random matrix theory.
entry.arxiv:comment: 40 pages, 2 figures v3: included a discussion on the convergence of numerical results and corrected typos

entry.title: Magpie: A Graphical Magnon Software
entry.summary: Magpie is a fully graphical linear spin-wave software which has its main focus on 3-d visualisation of magnetic models and magnon dispersion relations. The software is distributed under an open-source license and is written in high-performance, portable C++. Its modular architecture allows for a rapid development of new calculation modules and permits the inclusion into external applications. Included code generators ensure seamless interoperability with other linear spin-wave libraries.

entry.title: Rotating Vector Model predictions in millisecond pulsar magnetospheres with dipole and quadrupole field components
entry.summary: The rotating vector model (RVM) is widely used to interpret pulsar radio polarization under the assumption of a dipolar magnetic field. Motivated by tentative evidence for non-dipolar magnetic structure in millisecond pulsars provided by recent modeling of surface thermal X-ray pulsations, we examine how a global quadrupole component modifies position-angle (PA) behavior within the classical RVM framework. We numerically integrate magnetic field lines in static vacuum magnetospheres composed of a centered dipole component that is inclined with respect to the spin axis, and a centered quadrupole component aligned with it. We then compute the open field line regions (OFLRs), emission skymaps, and PA curves for a range of dipole inclinations, relative quadrupole strengths, and light cylinder radii corresponding to two trial spin periods of 1\,ms and 5\,ms. We find that quadrupole-modified magnetospheres produce a wide variety of PA behaviors and substantially alter the morphology and total area of OFLRs, with the OFLR area varying non-monotonically with quadrupole strength and, in some cases, exceeding that of the corresponding pure dipole. Depending sensitively on the field configuration and viewing geometry, three broad PA regimes can be distinguished: a) nearly dipolar PA swings that are largely insensitive to emission altitude; b) moderately distorted, altitude-dependent PA tracks that can bias dipolar RVM fits; and c) strongly dispersed PA behavior associated with emission from different OFLRs, which can remain incompatible with a single dipolar PA track even within narrow emission altitude ranges. These results demonstrate that dipole-like PA curves do not uniquely imply a purely dipolar magnetic field, while global quadrupole components alone are insufficient to reproduce the full complexity of observed millisecond pulsar PA profiles.

entry.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
entry.summary: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\simλ/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

entry.title: Variational Minimization of Almost Strong Zero Modes in Parafermionic Wires
entry.summary: Strongly interacting fermionic chains obeying a $Z_n$ symmetry can host topological phases with highly degenerate ground-state manifolds. The different ground states are connected by strongly bound fractionalized edge modes called parafermionic zero modes. While exactly preserved under time evolution at zero temperature, interactions lead to a destabilization of these modes at finite energy densities, and, given a generic Hamiltonian, obtaining the lifetime of these modes is often impossible as it requires knowledge of the full spectrum of the Hamiltonian or long time evolutions. Here, we propose a novel quantum-inspired algorithm that can be used to variationally search for these almost strong zero modes in generic parafermionic chain models. We demonstrate analytically and numerically that our ansatz faithfully reproduces the exact results and finds strongly bound parafermionic operators in the non-integrable Kitaev-Hubbard chain and chiral Potts model. Our results further allow us to verify the existence of a true strong zero mode in the symmetrical limit of the chiral Potts model for $Z_3$-parafermions.

entry.title: Spatial interference changes the symmetry class of a Josephson element
entry.summary: Spatial interference can break the inversion symmetry of an effective Josephson potential even in a laterally homogeneous junction with inversion-symmetric local energy. We derive a general criterion based on harmonic-dependent complex spatial form factors: a single local harmonic remains a shifted cosine, whereas multiple harmonics can acquire phases incompatible with any common inversion center, permitting cubic interactions and three-wave mixing. Phase reflection reverses all odd-order expansion coefficients about corresponding minima while preserving the even-order ones. For a capacitively shunted junction at fixed charging energy and arbitrary offset charge, it also preserves the complete quantum spectrum, enabling reversal of the odd nonlinear sector without spectral retuning. A centered cross junction with multiple local harmonics is one concrete example. Within the imposed-field model, a three-component magnetic field can generate an inversion-asymmetric effective potential, and reversing an odd number of field components exactly reflects it without changing the quantum spectrum of the capacitively shunted junction.

entry.title: Higher Dressing and Shift-Invariance in 4D Topological BF Theory
entry.summary: A characteristic feature of topological field theories is the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. In four-dimensional BF theory with cosmological term, we make this feature manifest by exactly reducing the finite non-Abelian shift symmetry. We do so by identifying a higher dressing field, a 1-form compensating the shift, allowing to build from first principles the composite shift-invariant field $\boldsymbol{B}=B-λ^{-1}F$. In terms of this dressed field, the dynamics becomes algebraic and sets $\boldsymbol{B}=0$, directly exposing the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. This provides the first explicit instance of the higher-form Dressing Field Method.

entry.title: Holographic Codes from Enriched Link Entanglement in Spin Networks
entry.summary: We introduce an enriched entanglement structure for spin networks, inspired by tensor-network constructions, in which internal links can carry a controlled and discrete amount of entanglement. In the spin-network picture, vertices are dual to simplices (more generally, to polyhedra) and links are dual to their faces. Standard spin-network gluing corresponds to fully identifying two simplices along a face, implemented by a maximally entangled, gauge-invariant singlet state on the corresponding link, while unglued faces correspond to links carrying no entanglement. Working on a complete graph, we promote this binary choice to a controlled and tunable structure by allowing each link to carry a variable amount of entanglement, interpolating between product states and the fully entangled singlet. The additional link variables therefore control not only the amount of entanglement but also the extent to which gauge invariance at internal links is preserved or broken, admitting an interpretation in terms of emergent edge-mode-like degrees of freedom. Within this framework, spin-network contraction defines a bulk-to-boundary map from link-entanglement data to boundary states. Adapting techniques developed in random tensor networks, we show that in a suitable large-spin regime the map is a co-isometry in expectation value, meaning that its adjoint preserves boundary inner products on average, up to the overall scale. Restricting to a code subspace defined by configurations in which links are either effectively glued or open, with small fluctuations around this pattern, the map becomes an isometry up to corrections that vanish in the large-spin limit. This yields a discrete and geometrically meaningful realization of holographic and error-correcting features within the spin-network Hilbert space.

entry.title: Bayesian exploration of weakly interacting models of dark matter admixed neutron stars based on multi-density constraints
entry.summary: We present a unified Bayesian analysis of Higgs-portal, neutron-decay, and axion-like-particle (ALP)-mediated dark matter in neutron stars within the single-fluid approximation. Using a common relativistic mean-field description of hadronic matter, we combine finite-nucleus and heavy-ion collision data, chiral effective field theory, NICER measurements of four pulsars, and GW170817. The individual dark-sector parameters remain weakly determined, while model-dependent shifts in nuclear skewness reveal the sensitivity of the inferred hadronic equation of state to the assumed dark-matter mechanism. The three scenarios yield substantially overlapping mass-radius and tidal-deformability predictions, with median maximum masses near $2.1\,M_\odot$. For $1.4\,M_\odot$ stars, the Higgs-portal model predicts higher $f$-mode frequencies and shorter damping times than the neutron-decay and ALP models, although their credible regions overlap. Comparison with three consistently reanalysed two-fluid models gives the largest Bayesian evidence to neutron decay: under the adopted priors, its Bayes factors relative to the Higgs-portal and two-fluid alternatives are approximately $24$-$37$, but only $2.2$ relative to ALP. This ranking concerns complete dark-matter models and does not establish a general preference for either fluid description or evidence for a dark component itself. Improved nuclear constraints and future gravitational-wave asteroseismology could provide complementary information to disentangle the hadronic and dark-sector contributions.

entry.title: Revisiting the Multiwavelength Data of GRB 240825A: Implications for a Two-Stage Central Engine and a Dusty Environment
entry.summary: Reanalyzing the multi-wavelength data of GRB 240825A, we identify two distinct prompt-emission episodes, i.e. an early, spectrally soft plateau and a subsequent bright, spectrally hard gamma-ray pulse. We show that this signature is consistent with a two-stage central engine model, in which the early soft plateau is powered by the dipolar spin-down radiation of a transient proto-magnetar, while the later hard pulse arises from a relativistic jet launched by fallback accretion onto the nascent black hole via the Blandford-Znajek mechanism. Adopting simulation-motivated initial black hole (BH) masses ($M_{\rm BH,0}$) and spins ($a_0$), our fits to the second episode yield total masses supplied to the post-collapse disk of $M_{\rm fb}=0.45$--$0.96 M_\odot$, fallback radii of $r_{\rm fb}=16.9$--$17.6 r_g$, and characteristic fallback timescales of $t_{\rm fb}=0.13$--$0.25$ s. The corresponding maximum inner accretion rates range from $0.18$ to $0.70 M_\odot \mathrm{s}^{-1}$, which is sensitive to $a_0$. Joint spectral fits with optical-X-ray afterglow data reveal a coupled temporal evolution of dust extinction and equivalent hydrogen column density. Incorporating this extinction evolution, an external forward-reverse shock model in a wind-like medium can account for the radio-to-GeV band afterglow data. Although ambient dust and the bright host galaxy may obscure any associated supernova, late-time optical reddening remains compatible with a supernova contribution. Applying the empirical relation between the prompt spectral peak energy and the SN peak bolometric magnitude gives an illustrative estimate of $M_{\rm bol,peak}=-19.46\pm0.35$ mag for a putative associated SN. These results support a two-stage evolution of the central engine and variable dusty environment of GRB 240825A, which provides insights into the nature of its progenitor.

entry.title: Effective Neutrino Mass and Apparent Phantom Crossing
entry.summary: Recent cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses have reached, and in some analyses fallen below, the minimum value implied by the normal mass ordering, suggesting a possible tension with neutrino-oscillation measurements. We investigate whether this discrepancy can be alleviated in a mass-varying-neutrino (MaVaN) cosmology in which a canonical pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) drives late-time cosmic acceleration and controls the masses of massive neutrinos through an exponential coupling. Using current cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and type Ia supernova data, we reconstruct the neutrino-mass evolution and show that the cosmologically inferred effective neutrino mass can fall below the present-day normal-ordering floor while remaining consistent with oscillation constraints. The same interaction produces a distinctive late-time signature, with 96% of the posterior expansion histories exhibiting a crossing of the apparent phantom divide, $w_{\rm app}=-1$, at $z_{\rm cross}=0.90^{+0.28}_{-0.13}$ at 68% C.L. The underlying scalar field nevertheless remains canonical, with $w_φ\geq -1$. Our results therefore show that neutrino mass variation can simultaneously alleviate the apparent neutrino-mass tension and generate the phantom-crossing behavior favored by current cosmological data, without introducing a phantom field or violating the null energy condition.

entry.title: Field Response of the Orbital Moment Probed by Integrated Magnetic Circular Dichroism
entry.summary: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is an optical probe of orbital time reversal symmetry breaking. Although frequency integrated MCD is related to the self-rotation contribution to orbital magnetization at zero field, its magnetic response generally differs from the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility. Here, we define the MCD susceptibility and derive general expressions for multiband systems using an electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariant approach. For insulators, the response contains contributions from the non-Abelian quantum metric, Berry curvature, and field induced interband mixing. For metals, a finite temperature Green function formulation separates the smooth response into Fermi sea and Fermi surface contributions. An independent Landau level calculation confirms the expressions for the zero-field MCD moment and its linear magnetic response. In a continuum model for twisted bilayer graphene, the MCD susceptibility vanishes within the charge neutrality gap, while the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility remains markedly diamagnetic. Near the gap edges, the orbital moment term dominates the response. Features near the van Hove energies are associated with density of states enhancement. These results clarify how the two susceptibilities reflect different orbital processes even for the same electronic structure and thus establish the MCD susceptibility as a distinct probe of orbital magnetic response.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages, 2 figures in main text; 33 pages, 4 figures in SM

entry.title: Zero modes and oscillatory instabilities of a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond field on a Schwarzschild background
entry.summary: We study equilibrium configurations and linear perturbations of a Lorentz-violating Kalb--Ramond field with a quartic symmetry-breaking potential and a non-minimal Riemann coupling on a fixed Schwarzschild background. The electric equilibrium is determined algebraically by a characteristic function that can develop a finite-radius double root. Approaching this configuration, the electric monopole response scales as $|\widehat e(ω,r_c)|\propto(γ_c-γ)^{-1/2}$, while the propagating monopole remains regular. For higher multipoles we obtain the exact axial zero-mode tower $ξ_{\ell n}=-(\ell+n+1)(\ell+n+2)/3$. At $\ell=1$ a complementary static mode gives a second low-frequency branch. Increasing the positive Riemann coupling causes two purely imaginary growing modes to collide and form an oscillatory unstable pair, with square-root real-part splitting. Independent numerical checks confirm that this behavior persists under changes of the equilibrium parameters. The corrected bare sign removes the monopole ghost, but a constrained high-momentum negative-energy direction remains on the asymptotically electric branch. We therefore distinguish the existence of classical growing modes from the stronger requirement of a positive-energy theory.

entry.title: Field-controlled breaking and restoration of parity-time symmetry in Josephson interference
entry.summary: Symmetry plays a fundamental role in determining the phases and physical properties of quantum matter. Controlling symmetry in mesoscopic superconducting devices provides a route to reconfigure their phase-coherent transport. Here we demonstrate symmetry-selective Josephson interferometry in lateral NbTi/PtTe$_{\text{2}}$/NbTi junctions by controlling the relative orientations of the current and magnetic field. From the supercurrent interference patterns, we construct a field-current symmetry map that identifies configurations exhibiting or violating the device-level parity ($\mathcal{P}$), time-reversal ($\mathcal{T}$) and their combined $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry. In the absence of an in-plane field, the junction exhibits a symmetric Fraunhofer pattern. An in-plane field parallel to the current produces a pronounced side-lobe asymmetry, whereas reversing both the current and the complete magnetic-field configuration restores a generalized $\mathcal{T}$ relation. Remarkably, orienting the in-plane field perpendicular to the current restores the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Fraunhofer response even at substantial field strengths. A microscopic model attributes this behavior to the interplay between disorder-induced potential variations and flux dipoles generated by in-plane-field Meissner focusing near the superconducting electrodes. Our results establish a reconfigurable Josephson interferometer in which the field-current geometry selects the symmetry operation being probed and switches the device between symmetry-broken and symmetry-restored interference states.
entry.arxiv:comment: Main text: 12 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary Information: 24 pages, 18 figures

entry.title: Probing the sensitivity of dark energy dynamics to equation of state parametrization flexibility
entry.summary: Allowing for greater low redshift flexibility through parametrizations such as CPL can lead to apparent deviations from $Λ$CDM. This motivates an investigation into whether such deviations reflect genuine dynamical dark energy or arise from parametrization choices. We investigate several dark energy parametrizations, including two phenomenological power law type extensions proposed here, the power law and modified power law forms, which allow greater low redshift flexibility (around $z \sim 1$) than CPL. Parametrizations permitting stronger evolution of the equation of state can exhibit enhanced phantom like behaviour at intermediate redshifts, but this feature is sensitive to the assumed functional form and its extrapolation. The statistical preference for such behaviour is modest, depends on the supernova sample, and is consistent across parametrizations, in agreement with recent analyses. The likelihood-ratio significance of this preference is $2.2$--$3.9σ$. Owing to limited data at $z > 2$, this is primarily driven by the equation of state in the range $1 \leq z \leq 2$, where parametrizations with enhanced flexibility, such as power law type forms, mildly improve the fit. The Akaike Information Criterion favours the DDE parametrizations over $Λ$CDM for all three supernova samples. The Bayesian Information Criterion mildly favours them for $+$Union3 and $+$DESY5 but disfavours them for $+$PantheonPlus.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages, 2 tables, 4 figures, accepted in EPJC

entry.title: Hybrid compact stars with finite strange quark mass and dark energy: implications for astrophysical observations
entry.summary: In this work, we present a detailed investigation of compact stars composed of deconfined quark matter, with finite strange quark mass ($m_s\neq0$), admixed with dark energy. The quark sector is described using the MIT bag model equation of state, while the dark energy component is assumed to satisfy a linear equation of state of the form $p^{de}=ωρ^{de}$, where $ω$ lies in the range $-1\leqω\leq-\frac{1}{3}$. The stellar configuration is studied within the Finch-Skea ansatz for the $g_{rr}$ metric potential. A coupling between the two components is introduced through the relation $ρ^{de}=βρ^Q$, where $β$ denotes the dark energy coupling parameter. From causality arguments, the admissible range of $β$ is constrained as $0<β<-\frac{1}{3ω}$. The structural properties of such compact stars are then analysed by varying $β$ within this range. Solution of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations yields a maximum mass of $2.012~ M_{\odot}$ with a corresponding radius of $\approx 11$ km. Notably, for a fixed $ω$, both the stellar mass and radius are found to decrease with increasing $β$. The model is further examined through causality, energy, and stability conditions, all of which are satisfied, thereby ensuring physical viability. Finally, the framework is applied to estimate radii of several compact star candidates identified as strange quark stars admixed with dark energy, with predictions showing close agreement with recent observational results.

entry.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice models
entry.summary: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/α^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

entry.title: No off-diagonal quantum focusing for Rényi divergences
entry.summary: The quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) is a mathematical expression of the idea that semiclassical gravity remains universally attractive. In its non-gravitational limit, the diagonal inequality is the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), which requires convexity of relative entropy with respect to the vacuum under null deformations. Rényi divergences generalize relative entropy, and positive results for the diagonal Rényi QNEC raise the question of whether they also satisfy the off-diagonal inequalities required by a full focusing principle. We show that classical correlations between distinct null generators obstruct this extension for any non-affine Rényi-type divergence satisfying data processing, tensor additivity, and matched classical-quantum conditioning.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages, 1 figure; v2: expanded introduction and discussion, and coherent-state SRD counterexample added

entry.title: Multifractality at the Integer Quantum Hall Transition: Acquittal of the Parabolic Law
entry.summary: Stationary wave functions at the integer quantum Hall transition are known to be multifractal, but the exact form of the multifractality spectrum has remained a subject of debate. While conformal field theory arguments predict a parabolic law, numerical simulations show deviations from parabolicity. We resolve this discrepancy by pointing out that powers of the local wave intensity fail to obey the Gaussian Free Field and Abelian Fusion Hypothesis assumed in earlier analysis. Rather, due to the non-Abelian nature of the underlying effective field theory, wave intensity correlators are dressed by insertions of background charge distributed uniformly in space. An exact expression for the $q$-moments of point-contact generated eigenstates is presented. Numerical tests are performed for the critical Chalker-Coddington network model on a rectangular torus. Our results are in precise agreement with the predictions of conformal symmetry realized as a level-4 current algebra.

entry.title: Finite-Time Bounds on Conformal Vacuum Energy Relaxation in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
entry.summary: We investigate finite time vacuum energy relaxation in conformally coupled scalar-tensor cosmology distinguishing the suppression accumulated along a physical trajectory from its asymptotic rate. For a canonical scalar with an exponential potential and constant conformal coupling, the autonomous system exhibits a stability exchange between scalar dominated and vacuum kinetic scaling solutions. In the power-law metric $f(R)=f_0R^n$ realization with $n>2$, the stable scalar dominated branch has a sustained relaxation rate below $0.579$ decades per Einstein frame e-fold. We additionally derive a finite time upper bound that accounts for depletion of the vacuum relative to the scalar potential. For the specified reference initial state $Ω_{Λ,i}=0.99$ and $Ω_{{\rm kin},i}=10^{-4}$, the bound excludes $60$ decades of suppression within $60$ e-folds throughout the $n>2$ family: $D_Λ(60)<47.7$. Numerical trajectories illustrate why this bound is conservative and why the transient contribution cannot be inferred from the final attractor alone. For the reference $f(R)\propto R^{2.14}$ solution, $D_Λ(60)\simeq7.53$ decades including a transient excess of about $3.27$ decades relative to uniform evolution at the asymptotic rate. The relaxed quantity is the dimensionless vacuum to gravitational scale hierarchy, its evolution also entails variation of the conformal frame Planck mass. The bounds are conditional on the homogeneous model and specified initial state, not a demonstration of complete cosmological viability.

entry.title: Circumbinary Discs as the Origin of Circumstellar Material around Interacting H-poor Supernovae and Fast Blue Optical Transients
entry.summary: Around 10 % of hydrogen-poor supernovae explode inside compact ($\sim 10^{15}$ cm), massive ($\sim 0.1 \ \mathrm{M_\odot}$) circumstellar material (CSM), signalling an episode of enhanced pre-explosion mass loss whose mechanism remains unclear. The extreme members of this population are considered to constitute some of the Fast Blue Optical Transients (FBOTs), which exhibit rapid rise times of $\sim$ few days and high peak luminosity $\sim 10^{44} \ \mathrm{erg}$. Recent binary evolution calculations show that the expansion of helium stars during their latest evolutionary stages can trigger a rapid but stable mass-transfer episode that can form a dense circumbinary disc (CBD) that may explain the observed dense CSM. However, a detailed, quantitative analysis of this process and the resulting CBD properties such as its mass, radius and density profile has not yet been undertaken. We present a set of models that solve the viscous evolution of such a CBD under time-dependent mass injection. We find that although the injected mass is initially sub-Keplerian, a lower ``accretion eigenvalue'' $χ$ prevents more mass from falling back onto the central binary. For our fiducial set of models, the CBD immediately prior to the explosion reaches a mass of $0.07-0.20 \ \mathrm{M}_\odot$, a half-mass radius of $640 - 4000 \ \mathrm{R}_\odot$, and an aspect ratio of $θ= H/R \sim 0.1$. We also show that the interaction between SN ejecta and the CBD can power some of the fastest-evolving interacting Type Ibc SNe that can be classified as FBOTs, such as SN 2018gep or SN 2019jc. Despite uncertainties in the model parameters, our results demonstrate that CBD formation triggered by rapid, stable mass transfer is a viable mechanism to explain the dense circumstellar environments observed around rapid, hydrogen-poor interacting SNe. entry.title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
entry.summary: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.

entry.title: Single-Particle Spectroscopy and Cross-Barrier Dynamics in Inhomogeneous Luttinger Liquids via Unified Field Bosonization Technique
entry.summary: The Unified Field Bosonization Technique (UFBT) is employed to investigate the single-particle properties of inhomogeneous Luttinger liquids containing localized clusters of impurities in the presence of forward-scattering interactions. Within this framework, fermionic two-point correlation functions are used to derive the leading-order singular contributions to the dynamical density of states (DDOS) and the cross-barrier tunneling conductance. The results reveal distinct power-law behaviours of the DDOS near the impurity cluster and in the far-field regime. The tunneling conductance exhibits a power-law temperature dependence, decreasing with decreasing temperature for repulsive interactions and increasing for attractive interactions, while remaining temperature-independent in the noninteracting limit. The impurity cluster modifies the amplitudes and spatial structure of these observables, whereas their characteristic power-law exponents are determined solely by the interaction parameters. The formulation accommodates arbitrary impurity strengths without requiring perturbative expansions in the impurity or interaction strengths. The characteristic scaling behaviour emerges directly from the fermionic correlation functions, without an explicit renormalization-group (RG) treatment of the impurity strength, while the weak-interaction limit recovers the leading perturbative correction to the tunneling response. These findings establish UFBT as a unified framework for describing local spectral properties and cross-barrier transport in inhomogeneous Luttinger liquids.

entry.title: Realistic Simulation of Valence-band Photoemission Spectra by using First-principles Calculations on the Basis of FLAPW Method
entry.summary: In order to reproduce experimental photoemission spectroscopy (PES) data by using band structure calculations with linearized augmented-plane-wave method, we developed a new method to calculate the atomic-subshell photoelectron differential cross section (PE-DCS) of the valence band. PE-DCS was calculated to be the sum of the products of the partial density of states (PDOS) and the photoionization differential cross section (PI-DCS) of each atomic subshell. To construct an appropriate PDOS beyond the conventional muffin-tin sphere (MTS) PDOS, we proposed a ``nearly-neutral atomic sphere", which can be defined as a natural extension of MTS. Although the calculational method for atomic-subshell PI-DCS was the standard Hartree-Fock-Slater method, we developed a new computer code in order to deal with the unoccupied electron shells in the ground state of isolated atoms up to $\sim$10 keV. Details of the PE-DCS calculations were examined by using two simple examples of Na metal and NaCl, and then, the method was applied to hard x-ray PES (HX-PES) data of CuAlO$_2$. The experimental spectra were satisfactorily reproduced, demonstrating the potential applications of our method to HX-PES spectra of many compounds.

entry.title: Polarized quantum effects in countable signals from intense laser - electron beam interactions
entry.summary: We investigate the feasibility of precision counting experiments based on laser-electron beam interactions to verify strong-field quantum electrodynamic effects, with particular emphasis on the stochastic nature of photon emission, photon polarization, and spin asymmetry. A precise Monte-Carlo model is developed using photon packets with multi-dimensional phase-space weighting, hierarchical-mesh cumulative distribution functions, and a variable time-step method. This model quantitatively reproduces the highest edge of the photon energy spectrum and the positron yield in the previous SLAC E-144 experiment. The quantized radiation back-reaction determines the highest edge tail and thus the positron yield for higher laser intensities. The spin asymmetry in photon emission and spin flip determines photon polarization in the high-energy tail, while that in pair production can be observed through the large-angle positron scattering. Our simulations predict that these effects depend on the combination of the electron-beam energy and the laser intensity, and that they could be verified in future ELI-NP experiments using sub-GeV electron beams and optical lasers with intensities ~10^22W/cm2.

entry.title: Anisotropic Friedel oscillations and isoperimetric transport in two-dimensional free lattice Fermi seas
entry.summary: Two physical consequences of the recent topological classification of 2d Fermi seas for free particles based on flat orbifolds $\mathbb{R}^2/Γ$ of discrete symmetry $Γ$, are explored. The first is a study of the spatial density behavior inside the mesoscopic window enclosed by the Fermi and (infinite) thermal lengths. It is shown that the single-particle density matrix exhibits a sharp directional anisotropy, encoding a real space diffraction pattern, {\it i.e.}, a Fraunhofer-like diagram of the Fermi sea, that reveals the point-group symmetries of the background lattice $Γ$ in the form of anisotropic Friedel oscillations. As examples, the special cases of the $p4m$ and $p6m$ crystallographic flat orbifolds are treated in some detail. The second physical consequence is the establishment of an explicit geometric correspondence between momentum-space packing and electrical transport. A mean-field expression for the longitudinal electrical conductivity $σ_{xx}$ as a function of the {\it isoperimetric parameter} $\cal{I}$ of the occupied orbifold domain by utilizing geometric measure theory is presented, satisfiying the scaling law $ σ_{xx} \propto 1/\sqrt{\cal{I}}$. The topological transport formula naturally incorporates the vanishing conductivity ($σ_{xx} \to 0$) of the previously described ``geometric insulators,'' promoting the isoperimetric parameter as an efficient descriptor for topological and geometric phases in conductors.

entry.title: Mapping the Contracting Corona in GS 1354-64 with Insight-HXMT and XRISM: Evolving X-ray Lags and Quenched Reflection across a Complete State Transition
entry.summary: We present a comprehensive broadband spectro-temporal analysis of the dynamically confirmed Galactic black hole transient GS 1354-64 during its 2025-26 outburst, using near-simultaneous observations from Insight-HXMT and XRISM. The high spectral resolution of the XRISM-Resolve microcalorimeter, coupled with the high-cadence broadband coverage of Insight-HXMT, reveals a dramatic evolution in the inner accretion geometry. During the early hard-intermediate state, the spectrum was dominated by a hot Comptonizing corona accompanied by relativistically broadened reflection features. As the outburst progressed, the corona cooled efficiently, the photon index steepened (Gamma >~ 2.5), and the reflection signatures, including the broad Fe K-alpha emission, were quenched, yielding a featureless, disk-dominated continuum. Concurrently, Type-C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) evolved from 0.25 Hz to 6.52 Hz. Cross-spectral timing analysis revealed that the broadband X-ray time lags changed from pronounced positive (hard) delays (~160 ms) at low frequencies to near zero as the source softened. However, a statistical analysis incorporating the measurement uncertainties shows that the broadband lags lack a significant monotonic correlation with the QPO frequency, photon index, or fractional rms. Instead, the scattered lag behavior suggests a competition between positive Comptonization delays and negative thermal reverberation. While the spectral softening and QPO acceleration provide strong evidence for a geometric contraction of the corona (whether interpreted via Lense-Thirring precession or the Two-Component Advective Flow (TCAF) paradigm), the broadband timing properties underscore the turbulent and inhomogeneous nature of the inner flow as the advancing Keplerian disk drives the source into the soft state.
